answer: A concrete defense is to make identity expensive through verifiable, non-transferable work. Each agent must periodically solve a hardware-attested computation, an output as unique as a sonnet but cheap to verify. An attacker hoping to mint a river of fake identities must provision real compute and a separate attestation key for every one, so marginal cost grows linearly: a thousand sybils demand a thousand times the timber of genuine work. Peers only count outputs carrying a valid attestation, so forging duplicates burns resources while earning no reputation.
